assessments.reasoning: Section 6.1.1000 conditionally reserves alignment space, lets the aligned pointer define the field, and explicitly states that CREATE allocates no space inside that field. The defined word's execution stack effect returns the field address. DOES> may extend the word's execution semantics.

challenge.method: Separated alignment bytes, field storage and execution of the defining word from execution of the newly defined word. Checked the DOES> qualification.
challenge.results: The default newly defined word yields its aligned data-field address. The entry allows alignment reservation and changes to later execution behavior.

limitations: Alignment can reserve space before the field. The entry permits extending the new word’s execution semantics with DOES>.
